sentences.text: Futabasaurus is a genus of plesiosaur, a marine reptile, belonging to the family Elasmosauridae.
This animal was approximately 7 meters long and weighed between 3 and 4 tonnes, though estimates suggest a possible range up to 9.2 meters.

It is distinguished from other elasmosaurids by a long distance between its eye sockets and nostrils, fused interclavicles and clavicles, a relatively long humerus, and slim femora with prominent muscle scars.
The species possessed a notably long distance between its eye sockets and nostrils.
Its clavicles and interclavicles were fused together, featuring a curved anterior edge.
The forelimb bone known as the humerus was relatively long compared to other species.
The femur of Futabasaurus was very thin and featured significant muscle impressions.
Futabasaurus holds the distinction of being the first elasmosaurid discovered in Japan.
The fossils were discovered by Tadashi Suzuki, who was a high school student at the time.
Many bones of the type specimen show evidence of predation or scavenging by the shark Cretalamna.
The genus Futabasaurus was formally described and named in 2006.
The type specimen was discovered in the Irimazawa Member of the Tamayama Formation within the Futaba Group in Fukushima Prefecture.
The genus name Futabasaurus honors the Futaba Group where it was found, while the species name suzukii honors the discoverer's family name, Suzuki.
Futabasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically in the Santonian age, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
The name Futabasaurus was also applied to an unnamed theropod dinosaur from Japan, which remains a nomen nudum and is distinct from the plesiosaur.
